name: Pennywise
label: Epitaph
lede: Four Hermosa Beach kids who played backyard parties turned a song about lost friends into one of punk's great singalongs, and kept going for thirty-plus years.

eras.title: Backyard parties in Hermosa Beach
eras.text: Four South Bay kids start as P.M.A. and play beach-town parties. Two EPs and a deal with Brett Gurewitz's Epitaph turn them into a label pillar.

years.cap: Pennywise performing at the Valley View Casino Center in San Diego, Californi... · Wikimedia
years.h: P.M.A. forms in Hermosa Beach
years.p: [[Jim Lindberg|430709c6-32a6-4829-83d6-0a794e7de31c]], [[Fletcher Dragge|0426363b-f0a6-4e2a-a467-d32efbed08a4]], Byron McMackin and Jason Thirsk start the band that becomes Pennywise; all but McMackin went to Mira Costa High School.
years.xp:
The band began as P.M.A., short for Positive Mental Attitude, playing the beach-town party circuit around Hermosa. Thirsk on bass wrote many of the earliest songs.

According to Wikipedia, the name changed to Pennywise before the band signed to a label.

years.h: Jason Thirsk writes Bro Hymn for three lost friends
years.p: Thirsk wrote the song as a tribute to Tim Colvin, Carlos Canton and Tom Nichols; Nichols drowned at Hermosa Beach Pier in 1988.

years.h: Two EPs: A Word from the Wise and Wildcard
years.p: Pennywise put out their first two EPs on their own before any label deal.

years.h: Pennywise: the Epitaph debut
years.p: Signed to [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]] guitarist Brett Gurewitz's Epitaph, the band release their first album, with Bro Hymn on it.

years.h: Jim Lindberg leaves six months after the debut
years.p: He left the band, citing a lack of motivation and security in local rock bands; he rejoined in late 1992.

eras.title: Rejoin, Unknown Road, About Time
eras.text: Lindberg is back and the band settle into their sound. About Time gives them their first Billboard 200 entry.

years.h: Lindberg returns; Randy Bradbury briefly on bass
years.p: Thirsk moved to vocals for a time in 1992, with Randy Bradbury first joining on bass, then leaving before he came back in 1996.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Bradbury as bassist in 1992 and again from 1996. Sources on the exact shape of the 1992 shuffle are thin.

years.h: Unknown Road arrives on Epitaph
years.p: The second album, made after Lindberg's return, came out in August 1993.

years.h: About Time lands on June 13
years.p: The record peaked at number 96 on the Billboard 200 and number 55 on Australia's ARIA chart, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Losing Jason Thirsk
eras.text: The band's bassist dies in July 1996. They carry on, dedicate Full Circle to him, and become a Warped Tour staple.

years.h: Bassist Jason Thirsk dies at 28
years.p: He had left the band to recover from alcoholism; Wikipedia reports he died by suicide from a gunshot wound, and that he had suffered from depression.
years.xp:
Thirsk was born December 25, 1967, in Hermosa Beach. According to Wikipedia, his girlfriend found him about a day after his death.

The band dedicated its Warped Tour 1996 shows to him.

years.h: Randy Bradbury takes over on bass
years.p: Bradbury replaced Thirsk in 1996 and has held the job since.

years.h: Full Circle is dedicated to Thirsk
years.p: Bro Hymn is re-recorded as Bro Hymn (Tribute), with Thirsk's brother Justin on drums and vocals for the track.

years.h: Straight Ahead
years.p: Fifth album on Epitaph.

years.h: Fletcher Dragge barricades the Loveline studio door
years.p: Drunk during a KROQ Weenie Roast promotion, the 6-foot-5 guitarist blocked hosts Adam Carolla and Dr. Drew in; police came but no charges followed, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Land of the Free? with Gurewitz co-writing
years.p: Epitaph boss Brett Gurewitz co-wrote Who's on Your Side, and the band played Vans Warped 2001.

eras.title: Mid-career Epitaph years
eras.text: From the Ashes gives them their highest initial chart entry, and a free MySpace download brings a wider audience.

years.h: From the Ashes charts at number 54
years.p: Its highest initial chart position, per Wikipedia.

years.h: The Fuse is out in Europe first
years.p: The album reached Europe on June 27 and North America on August 9.

years.h: Reason to Believe goes free on MySpace
years.p: The band gave away the album as a MySpace download, which Wikipedia says drew over 400,000 downloads; it peaked at number 98 on Billboard.

years.h: Reason to Believe
years.p: Their ninth album.

eras.title: Lindberg out, Zoli in, Lindberg back
eras.text: The band's singer walks away to make a documentary and a side band, Ignite's Zoli Teglas steps in, then a back injury sends the door open again.

years.h: Lindberg announces his exit
years.p: Jim Lindberg left in August 2009 and formed The Black Pacific while filming The Other F Word, based on his book Punk Rock Dad.
years.xp: The documentary, released in 2011 by most accounts, follows punk dads. Wikipedia dates the film to 2014; sources disagree.

years.h: Ignite's Zoli Teglas is named the new singer
years.p: The Orange County hardcore vocalist was announced as Lindberg's permanent replacement.

years.h: All or Nothing with Teglas
years.p: The only Pennywise album he sang on.

years.h: Teglas hurts his back at a German show
years.p: He needed emergency surgery and asked to leave, opening the way for Lindberg's return.

years.h: Lindberg is back, announced on KROQ
years.p: He said he wanted the internal conflict to stop, adding that a song about unity could not sit beside a band fractured down the middle.

eras.title: Family back together
eras.text: A Palladium show celebrates 25 years, and Yesterdays digs into the earliest Thirsk-era songs.

years.h: 25th anniversary at the Hollywood Palladium
years.p: Lindberg described feeling enormous relief that the family was back together, comparing the split to a divorce that touched friends too.

q: We didn't care about anything except playing backyard parties.
years.h: Yesterdays revisits songs from the backyard-party days
years.p: Many were written by Jason Thirsk before 1996; Lindberg says he wanted a raw, unambitious sound.

years.h: Never Gonna Die comes out
years.p: The band's twelfth album, still with Dragge, McMackin, Bradbury and Lindberg.
